implemented.rule: An AI agent holds only explicitly assigned scope; removal terminates access.
implemented.before: getAllowedGroupIds returned [fallback_group_id] for an agent absent from the registry and getDefaultGroupId returned the fallback, so any unlisted agent silently held allura-system. isAgentAllowedGroupId therefore returned true for the fallback tenant.
implemented.after: An unlisted agent gets an empty allowlist, every isAgentAllowedGroupId check is false, and getDefaultGroupId refuses rather than inventing a tenant. fallback_group_id is retained for registry-shape compatibility and is no longer consulted as a grant.
implemented.red: 4 failed / 3 passed in the registry describe block of src/__tests__/epic30-agent-explicit-assignment.test.ts — exactly the default-allow paths. (An earlier draft of this receipt said 4/2; the shipped block has 7 tests.)
implemented.productionConsumer: NONE. Correction recorded after independent review: the registry module's only importers are three test files. No route, MCP tool, middleware, script or plugin consults it for an access decision, so this is latent-API hardening rather than an enforced control, and the previous fallback was likewise never a live grant. The live agent-scope grain is the mcp_tokens row.
implemented.cacheGap: loadRegistry caches by path for the process lifetime and nothing invalidates it outside tests, so editing the YAML to remove an agent leaves the stale grant live until reload or restart. Two tests pin both directions: removal terminates access after reloadRegistry, and removal without reload does not.
implemented.renamed: The export is getAgentAllowedGroupIds, not getAllowedGroupIds, because src/lib/workspace/boundary.ts exports a same-named function whose empty array means ALLOW-ANY. Here an empty array means DENY; colliding names could invert an access decision.
implemented.typedRefusal: getDefaultGroupId raises a typed AgentAssignmentMissingError rather than a bare Error, and the test matches the class, so rewording the message cannot silently disable the assertion.

implemented.rule: Least privilege: an agent credential with no assignment reaches nothing.
implemented.before: applyPrincipalToArgs refused a principal with no verified workspace binding for only memory_search, memory_get and memory_list. Every other tool fell through with a tenant-only scope and no injected workspace, so memory_delete, memory_update, memory_export, memory_restore, memory_promote, audit_query_events and governance_audit_log ran tenant-wide on the ABSENCE of an assignment.
implemented.after: A delegated mcp_token principal with no verified workspace binding is refused on every tool. mcp_tokens.workspace_id is NOT NULL in the schema, so a genuinely minted agent credential always carries one; only the optional TypeScript shape allowed it to go missing.
implemented.scopedDeliberately: The ALL-TOOL refusal is restricted to authMethod === 'mcp_token' because widening it breaks the AC-10 shared-token compatibility contract in src/__tests__/mcp-auth-adversarial.test.ts. The earlier claim that service_identity and dev_local are 'fenced out of production' and 'carry their own explicit tenant allowlists' was WRONG and is withdrawn: dev_local is fenced, but the HTTP shared-token service_identity path is not, and shared-token tenants default to ['allura-system'] with roles ['viewer'] requiring no explicitness.
implemented.red: 7 tools failed to deny: memory_delete, memory_update, memory_export, memory_restore, memory_promote, audit_query_events, governance_audit_log.
implemented.green: 20/20 in the new policy test; 83/83 with mcp-auth-adversarial included.
implemented.regressionIntroducedAndFixed: The first attempt gated the refusal solely on authMethod === 'mcp_token', which REMOVED the pre-existing refusal of memory_search/memory_get/memory_list for service_identity and dev_local. Independent review caught it: that turned an audited deny (PrincipalAuthError CONFIG_MISSING, logged as decision 'deny') into an audited allow, with the second-layer requireVerifiedWorkspaceScope throwing an unaudited plain Error. Repaired: those three reads now refuse for EVERY auth method, exactly as before, and the all-tool refusal applies additionally to mcp_token. A regression test pins the restored read refusal.
implemented.scopeObjectGuard: The workspaceId conjunct on scope construction is retained. Dropping it would have emitted a PRESENT but workspace-less scope object for the unfenced shared-token path where the key was previously absent — inert against every current consumer (all read scope?.workspace_id) but a latent false positive for the next one that treats a truthy scope as verified.

deliberatelyNotImplemented.item: Founder all-access for the three named founders
deliberatelyNotImplemented.reason: Correction 1 conflicts with three already-approved decisions: contract §2 ('roles, including admin, authorize administrative actions only'), approval-packet decision 2 ('owner-private content has no administrator override') and accepted epic default 3 (no administrator override in MVP). It can be read as founders being implicit members of every Faith Meats project (compatible) or as founders overriding owner-private content (incompatible). Implementing the second reading by inference would silently remove the owner-only guarantee the rest of the contract rests on. Recorded as an open decision in contract §10.2; one written choice from the owner is required.
deliberatelyNotImplemented.ownerAction: Choose reading (a) project-scope membership or (b) content override, in writing.
deliberatelyNotImplemented.supersededBy: RESOLVED later the same day. The owner chose reading (a): founder status is project eligibility/membership and never overrides owner-private visibility. The ownerAction recorded alongside this entry is closed. The non-override half needed no code because owner-private already resolves by owner identity with no role branch, and a regression guard now pins it; the eligibility half remains unimplemented pending project-grained membership. See evidence/epic30-founder-eligibility-not-override-2026-09-28.json.

deliberatelyNotImplemented.reason: No project-grained authority exists. The projects table is tenant-scoped with tenant-wide RLS and no workspace_id; project_id is an organising column on lanes, work_items and the messaging tables and carries no authority. There is no project_members table, and no membership, approval or credential table has a principal-type discriminator, so no policy can currently say 'deny because the principal is an agent'. The finest grain that exists is tenant plus workspace, with department membership inside it. Corrections 1 and 2 are therefore enforced at the grain that exists; the project grain is an open implementation gap recorded in contract §10.3.
deliberatelyNotImplemented.ownerAction: Scope and schedule project-grained authority as its own work; it is not inside the current Epic 30 slice.

deliberatelyNotImplemented.item: Reducing the four-tenant grants held by gilliam, troy and openwork
deliberatelyNotImplemented.reason: These are explicit assignments, so they satisfy the 'never automatic' rule, but four tenants each is unlikely to be least privilege. Reducing them removes access from running agents. Removal is an owner decision and was not taken unilaterally.
deliberatelyNotImplemented.ownerAction: Confirm or reduce each agent's tenant list.

knownGapsRecorded: The agent registry module has no production consumer; it is latent-API hardening, not an enforced control.

The agent registry is a YAML file, not a governed table: assignment and removal leave no audit trail and terminate no live session, and its process-lifetime cache means an edit does not take effect until reload or restart.

OPEN RISK, not closed: the HTTP shared-token service_identity path is production-reachable and unfenced, carries no workspace binding, and audit_query_events, governance_audit_log and memory_export filter on group_id alone — tenant-wide audit and export reach. Widening the refusal breaks the AC-10 contract, so this is referred to the policy owner as a blocking risk rather than fixed here.
Membership and project revocation timing remains an unmeasured target; only credential revocation is proved live.
